evidence.source: 羅忱烈, “楚「些」字的形音問題”
evidence.text: The author argues that the *Zhao Hun* line-final particle was probably not written with the graph 些 in its earliest form. The character’s first appearance in surviving lexicographic records is uncertain; the article identifies an entry in the sixth-century *Sanwu lü* as an early record and describes later Tang and Song dictionary attestations. It discusses proposals that 些 arose through graphic corruption or popular writing of 告, but does not establish an early graphic chain.
evidence.title: 楚「些」字的形音問題

evidence.source: 羅忱烈, “楚「些」字的形音問題”
evidence.text: The article distinguishes the *Zhao Hun* rhyme particle from later dictionary pronunciations and meanings. It reports the *Guangyun* reading 苏贺切 for the Chu particle and discusses a competing analysis connecting 些 with 告 and the demonstrative/particle senses of 斯 and 此. These remain competing historical explanations; the article does not demonstrate a secure spoken-word-to-graph chronology for the *Chuci* text.
evidence.title: 楚「些」字的形音問題

evidence.source: 中國哲學書電子化計劃, 楚辭疏: 五
evidence.text: The transmitted *Zhao Hun* repeatedly places 些 at line ends, for example “魂兮歸來，南方不可以止些.” The commentary records the reading 苏贺反 and explains 些 as a particle, adding that it was a Chu custom. This witnesses the transmitted graph and an inherited gloss, not the original manuscript spelling or the poem’s composition date.
evidence.kind: primary text in later annotated edition
evidence.title: 楚辭疏 : 五

evidence.source: 教育部《國語辭典簡編本》
evidence.text: The entry gives xiē and suò as readings. It describes suò as a sentence-final particle expressing interrogative, exclamatory, or prohibitive tone, citing the *Chuci* *Zhao Hun* example “魂兮歸來，南方不可以止些.” This documents current lexicographic treatment, not the historical derivation of the particle.
evidence.title: <些> 辭典檢視 - 教育部《國語辭典簡編本》2021

evidence.source: Wiktionary, 些
evidence.text: The page lists the modern graph composition as 此 over 二 and groups 些 in the 此 phonetic series, giving Zhengzhang (2003) Old Chinese forms *saːls, *sjaːl, and *seːs. These are secondary compilations and do not by themselves prove either an original 此 phonetic role or 二 semantic role; the page’s historical-form images were not used to establish a developmental sequence.
evidence.title: 些 - Wiktionary, the free dictionary

evidence.field: earliest lexicographic record; competing graphic histories
evidence.text: The article says the earliest surviving dictionary record it identifies is the sixth-century Yupian entry under 此, with readings 息計切 and 息箇切 and glosses 此也、辭也. It reports proposals that 些 is a popular or corrupted spelling related to another graph, including 告, and does not establish a secure early graphic chain. The author argues that the transmitted Zhao Hun particle spelling may postdate the poem; this is the author's analysis, not a settled manuscript fact.
evidence.title: 楚「些」字的形音問題

evidence.source: 羅忱烈, “楚「些」字的形音問題”
evidence.text: The article distinguishes the Zhao Hun line-final particle from dictionary readings. It reports Guangyun 蘇箇切 for the particle tradition and discusses a competing reading argument based on comparison with other Chu-ci line-final particles. These historical proposals do not demonstrate that 此 was the phonetic source of the particle or establish a sound borrowing from a separately named object.

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.field: 形體資料表; record of component analysis
evidence.text: The entry identifies the received Shuowen Daxu Xinfu form as composed from 此 and 二, and records variant forms including 㱔, 𡭟 and 呰. It reports no available oracle-bone, bronze, or several other early paleographic source records in its form table. This supports the received form description, not a demonstrated semantic role for 二 or phonetic role for 此 in the original formation.
evidence.title: [A00056] 些 - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

evidence.source: Ministry of Education, Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants
evidence.text: The dictionary relates 𡭟 to 些 through later dictionary citations glossing it as 少也, and records 呰 as a variant used for the particle sense. It notes that 呰 also exists as a distinct character meaning 苛, formed from 口 and 此 according to Shuowen. These later variant records do not supply an ancient formation sequence for 些.
evidence.title: [A00056] 些 - Ministry of Education《Dictionary of Chinese Character Variants》2024

context.provenance: Base evidence consists of imported local JSONL excerpts. Source names identify upstream datasets; extraction may lose sense and language boundaries. Further external evidence and research activity are documented separately in the dossier.
editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.

gaps: The supplied dossier’s Shuowen gloss (“語辭也。見《楚辭》。从此从二。其義未詳。”) was not independently verified against an accessible primary *Shuowen* edition. It is historical testimony, not confirmed graphic etymology.

No securely inspectable oracle-bone, bronze, or manuscript forms establishing the formation of 些 or a chronological 此+二 development were found. Semantic and phonetic roles of 此 and 二 remain unproven; no component-origin relationship should be asserted from shape alone.

Whether the early *Zhao Hun* particle was originally written as 些, 告, 只, or another graph remains disputed. The scholarly article argues for later substitution/popular spelling, while the transmitted text and later dictionaries use 些.
No early lexical path from the particle sense to the modern quantifier ‘a few/some’ was established. Do not infer that semantic chronology from modern gloss lists.

The sound of 此 is not an independently established historical explanation of the particle’s pronunciation. No whole-graph loan claim or source-word/object analysis is supported by the inspected evidence.

The official Unicode U+4E9B record was attempted but unavailable (cache miss); local Unihan row supplied in the packet gives xiē. No local Baxter–Sagart entry was found by character search; historical readings cited above are Zhengzhang’s system, not Baxter–Sagart.

The article’s scan text has OCR corruption in places. Its readable argument supports uncertainty and competing proposals, but finer palaeographic details require inspection of the page image or cited editions.

No independently inspected early manuscript, excavated inscription, oracle-bone, or bronze form of 些 was established. The received 此+二 analysis is recorded by the Shuowen tradition, but the semantic and phonetic roles of those parts remain unproven.

The earliest record discussed by the inspected secondary scholarly article is a sixth-century Yupian dictionary entry; no direct primary scan of that entry was opened in this session. Exact first use of the graph remains uncertain.
The Zhao Hun transmitted particle spelling and its original graphic form remain disputed. The article's 告-related corruption/popular-spelling account is an analysis, not an established sequence.
No securely dated lexical bridge from the line-final particle use to the modern quantifier sense ‘some/few’ was verified. The sources inspected do not establish that semantic chronology.

No evidence establishes an independent ancient pronunciation for 此 as the origin of 些's particle reading, nor a whole-graph loan from a depicted object's name. No object-name or borrowing claim is made.

The official Unicode U+4E9B lookup returned an internal error. Current xiē is present in the supplied local Unihan row, but external click-through verification failed. Baxter–Sagart comparison could not be completed from an exact local row for 些.

No suitable historical glyph image with verified identity and reuse provenance was found. The exact Commons candidate is a modern stroke-order illustration; Xiaoxuetang yielded no character-specific record in the inspected result.

limitations.text: No verifiable historical glyph is available to illustrate 些: the record discussed for the sixth-century Yupian has no directly inspected image here, and the transmitted 楚辭 spelling does not establish the poem’s original graph. The accepted 此-plus-二 analysis therefore cannot be shown as a verified historical form.
